purpose: Rc process-graph parity matrix for Star 9
rule: Pipelines, jobs, rfork, notes, and wait must be represented through Star 9 tasks, fd tables, pipes, namespaces, env files, and device files. Host shell side channels are not acceptable.

layers.portable_evaluator: crates/star9-rc keeps deterministic captured execution for fake hosts, pure built-ins, browser-limited hosts, and hosts without a streaming execution provider.
layers.star9_adapter: crates/star9-shell/src/rc.rs implements process-graph hooks over Star 9 task, fd, pipe, namespace, and execution-registry surfaces.
layers.provider_execution: Native-host Star 9 rc can execute external WASI stages, opt-in native stages, and registered JS/WASM stages through provider-backed task/fd graphs. Browser rc can run worker-backed graph-compatible stages through the JS shell provider with bounded stdin/stdout buffering over Star 9 worker tasks.

features.notes: The reusable rc crate exposes host-neutral graph specs and records without depending on Star 9 runtime types.
The Star 9 adapter creates per-stage task records, standard fds, and selected pipe fd bindings under .rc/graphs.

Native-host rc starts two-stage and linear multi-stage WASI pipelines, registered JS/WASM worker stages, and opt-in native stages concurrently where handlers support streaming. It installs pipe/file/stdio descriptors into task fd tables, closes writer endpoints for EOF, reads final stdout/stderr from task fds, and aggregates pipeline status. Unregistered JS/WASM modules still fall back to the portable command path instead of pretending a provider exists.

Executable <{} and >{} forms use provider-backed process-substitution graphs when a host graph provider can run the stage. Pure built-ins and unsupported/browser-limited stages keep evaluator data paths for portability, while the Star 9 adapter still creates task/fd graph records that expose the intended pipe endpoint.

Pure built-ins keep deterministic job records. External WASI/native/registered-JS graph jobs can run in provider threads and wait through rc job ids. Provider-backed graphs expose persistent kind/job/tasks/notes/state/status/ctl files under .rc/graphs. Completed graphs can be cleaned up by writing cleanup or close to ctl; running graphs require cancellation first.

Captured stdout/stderr redirection, fd dup/close, process-substitution sink handling, and provider stdio descriptor installation are implemented. Provider-backed executable stages can carry file read/write/append redirects, fd close, selected pipe fds, and process substitution pipe endpoints into task fd descriptors. Arbitrary nested fd graphs and exact Plan 9 process graph concurrency for every edge form remain provider-depth work.
rfork e is accepted through the host boundary. Namespace/env/fd/process-group sharing flags remain precisely rejected until Star 9 has matching task scope controls.

sigexit and rc note functions work. The Star 9 adapter broadcasts notes through #signal/data where present. Active provider-backed jobs are marked with deterministic signal:<note> status, graph state/status files, notes, wait results, and task exits. Browser worker graph controllers can terminate owned workers. WASI/native/registered in-process handlers still expose precise hard-cancel boundaries unless the provider supplies an interrupt primitive.

Browser rc keeps the deterministic evaluator for pure rc and unsupported graph shapes. Graph-compatible worker stages such as worker module.mjs and direct .js/.mjs/.wasm module commands can run through browser Worker tasks with bounded stdin/stdout handoff, wait, task exit observation, and best-effort graph files under .rc/graphs. This is not raw browser TCP or OS process execution.

Native Star 9 rc graph ctl accepts status, hold, release, cancel <note>, cleanup, and close. Cleanup unbinds graph mounts after completion and is idempotent from the caller perspective. Browser graph files are diagnostic best-effort surfaces because the browser provider is async and facade-host dependent.

import! services use cross-document MessagePort 9P. ws!/wss! services can be mounted through a configured WebSocket 9P provider. webtransport! addresses parse and route through the same provider hook, but the default SystemElement reports WebTransport provider-missing until a concrete provider is installed.
